result.instructions:
How to write rich text in Blok:
Rich text is a list of segments: { text, marks? } or { embed, marks? }. A plain string is plain text, HTML tags included.
Marks: bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, code, sup, sub, highlight, color, background, link, and tag:<name> for a custom inline tool. sup and sub cannot share a run.
highlight alone is stored as background "yellow"; with a background, as that background. color and background take a preset: "gray", "brown", "orange", "yellow", "green", "blue", "purple", "pink", "red". Hex, rgb and hsl are stored as the nearest preset. A CSS colour name is lowercased and kept, and so is var(--name). Other syntaxes (oklch, lab, hwb, color()) are dropped, as are a transparent colour and a white or dark-grey page background.
A link needs href. With no target or rel it gets target "_blank" and rel "nofollow"; an "#anchor" href gets target "_self". A target or rel you give is kept, but in the editor a host link config replaces both.
Embeds: { equation: { expression } } is inline LaTeX; { page: { id } } mentions a page: id is the pageId in a page block's data, not the block id.
text.format with unset ["*"] clears every mark; "tag:*" clears every custom mark.
markdown.insert cannot write underline, sup, sub, highlight or colours: insert the text, then use text.format.

Rules for editing a Blok document:
- Call blok_read when you need blocks, text or data you do not have. Address blocks by the ids it returns.
- Rich text is segments, not Markdown and not HTML. To add Markdown, use the markdown.insert command.
- When the blok_execute schema lists a command's full arguments, use them. Otherwise call blok_describe with { command } before using it for the first time. Call it with { tool } for a block type's data.
- Someone may be typing in the document at the same time, so its text can change between your calls.
- On a STALE error, call blok_read again and retry with fresh ids and text.
- A CORRECTED warning means Blok changed your command. Check the result is what you meant.
- Change only the blocks the request is about. To add something, insert a new block; do not convert or rewrite a nearby block to get it.
- Put related edits in one blok_execute call.
- A page block's data.pageId is the id of its sub-page document; open it with blok_open to write inside it.

tools.name: blok_list_documents
tools.description: Lists Blok documents you may open. blok_open without documentId runs this listing itself, so you rarely need it. query matches part of document ids and titles, not their content; when nothing matches, it lists every document and sets queryMatched: false. Returns supported: false when the document source cannot list.

query.description: Matches part of a document id or title. It does not search the text inside documents.

tools.name: blok_open
tools.description: Opens a Blok document and returns a handle for blok_read, blok_describe, blok_execute and blok_close. Called without documentId, it opens a document only when exactly one fits: with no query, the only document there is; with a query, the one document whose id or title equals query (case and outer spaces ignored). Then it returns that documentId and title. Otherwise it opens nothing and returns the documents to choose from, listed the way blok_list_documents lists them; open one by its documentId. In stored mode an unknown documentId opens a new, empty document (exists: false), so pass only ids you were given or saw listed. A page block's data.pageId is the documentId of that sub-page: open it to read or edit the sub-page. The block id is not. mode "auto" joins the live room when one is configured, else edits the stored document. Pass write: true if you will edit; a read-only handle refuses blok_execute. unavailableCommands names the blok_execute commands this handle refuses, if any; do not send them. Pass view with blok_read arguments, e.g. view: {}, to get the document back in the same call. A handle expires after 10 minutes without a call; then open again. Write rich text with commands such as text.format or markdown.insert. Never put Markdown or HTML into block data.

query.description: Without documentId: the exact id or title of the document to open.

oneOf.description: A block id, or "$" plus the ref of a block an earlier command created.

items.description: A block id, or "$" plus the ref of a block an earlier command created.

tools.name: blok_close
tools.description: Closes a handle. In live mode it leaves the room and reports work the server had not acknowledged. In stored mode every blok_execute already saves, so closing is not needed to save; it only frees the handle.

tools.name: blok_read
tools.description: Read the document as a tree of blocks with ids, types and text. Read before you edit, and again after a STALE error.

oneOf.description: A block id, or "$" plus the ref of a block an earlier command created.

items.description: A block id, or "$" plus the ref of a block an earlier command created.

tools.name: blok_describe
tools.description: Look up what you can do. With no arguments it lists tools and commands. Pass { tool } or { command } to get the argument schema.

tools.name: blok_execute
tools.description: Run a batch of commands. Either all of them land or none do. Use block ids from blok_read. To add several text blocks at once (headings, paragraphs, lists, code), use one markdown.insert. The schema has the full arguments for block.convert, block.delete, block.insert, block.move, doc.setIcon, doc.setTitle, markdown.insert, text.format, text.replace. Call blok_describe for any other command's arguments. Its result lists the changed blocks with their data as they now read, so you can check your work without blok_read.

type.description: A block tool: paragraph, header, list, toggle, callout, quote, code. A variant sets these data fields; the tool's other required fields still go in data: header {level: 1|2|3|4|5|6, isToggleable: true}, list {style: "unordered"|"ordered"|"checklist"}.

A block tool: paragraph, header, list, table, toggle, callout, database, database-row, divider, spacer, table_of_contents, quote, code, image, file, audio, video, column_list, column, tabs, tab, embed, bookmark, page-link. A variant sets these data fields; the tool's other required fields still go in data: header {level: 1|2|3|4|5|6, isToggleable: true}, list {style: "unordered"|"ordered"|"checklist"}.

data.description: Rich-text fields take what text.replace "with" takes.

markdown.description: Gives bold, italic, strikethrough, inline code and links. Markdown has no syntax for underline, sup, sub, highlight or colours, and their HTML stays literal: set them with text.format. Call describe({ command: 'markdown.insert' }) for the rest.

unset.description: To remove a mark, list it here. "*" clears all, "tag:*" custom marks; set then applies.

with.description: Plain text (HTML tags stay literal), or rich-text segments. Never Markdown.

id.description: Later commands use this id as is, no "$".

marks.description: Formatting on one run. Unknown keys drop, except custom `tag:<name>` marks.

sup.description: Not with sub on one run.

highlight.description: Stored as background "yellow" unless background is set.

color.description: "gray", "brown", "orange", "yellow", "green", "blue", "purple", "pink", "red". Hex, rgb, hsl snap to the nearest; names and var() stay; other syntaxes drop.

id.description: A block id, or "$" plus the ref of a block an earlier command created.

highlight alone is stored as background "yellow"; with a background, as that background. color and background take a preset: "gray", "brown", "orange", "yellow", "green", "blue", "purple", "pink", "red". Hex, rgb and hsl are stored as the nearest preset. A CSS colour name is lowercased and kept, and so is var(--name). Other syntaxes (oklch, lab, hwb, color()) are dropped, as are a transparent colour and a white or dark-grey page background.
A link needs href. With no target or rel it gets target "_blank" and rel "nofollow"; an "#anchor" href gets target "_self". A target or rel you give is kept, but in the editor a host link config replaces both.
Embeds: { equation: { expression } } is inline LaTeX; { page: { id } } mentions a page: id is the pageId in a page block's data, not the block id.
text.format with unset ["*"] clears every mark; "tag:*" clears every custom mark.
markdown.insert cannot write underline, sup, sub, highlight or colours: insert the text, then use text.format.

Rules for editing a Blok document:
- Call blok_read when you need blocks, text or data you do not have. Address blocks by the ids it returns.
- Rich text is segments, not Markdown and not HTML. To add Markdown, use the markdown.insert command.
- When the blok_execute schema lists a command's full arguments, use them. Otherwise call blok_describe with { command } before using it for the first time. Call it with { tool } for a block type's data.
- Someone may be typing in the document at the same time, so its text can change between your calls.
- On a STALE error, call blok_read again and retry with fresh ids and text.
- A CORRECTED warning means Blok changed your command. Check the result is what you meant.
- Change only the blocks the request is about. To add something, insert a new block; do not convert or rewrite a nearby block to get it.
- Put related edits in one blok_execute call.
- A page block's data.pageId is the id of its sub-page document; open it with blok_open to write inside it.
